contentChunks.htmlValue: Usage

Sliders are used to select values along a track. They’re ideal for adjusting settings such as volume and brightness, or changing the intensity of image filters.

Sliders can use icons or labels to represent a numeric or relative scale.

contentChunks.footer: Use sliders to pick a value from a range, like volume loudness
contentChunks.altText: Sound settings screen with continuous sliders labeled call volume and alarm volume.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Changes made with sliders must take effect immediately, so people can understand the effects of their selection as they're moving the slider.

contentChunks.footer: Selection changes are immediate
contentChunks.altText: The brightness slider changes the screen’s brightness in real time.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
There are three different variants of sliders: standard, centered, and range:

Standard sliders select one value from a range of values. Use this when the slider should start from zero or the beginning of a sequence.

contentChunks.footer: Horizontal standard slider
contentChunks.altText: Horizontal standard slider with an end stop indicator.

contentChunks.footer: Vertical standard slider
contentChunks.altText: Vertical standard slider  with an end stop indicator.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Centered sliders select a value from a positive and negative value range. Use this when zero, or the default value, is in the middle of the range.

contentChunks.footer: Horizontal centered slider
contentChunks.altText: Horizontal centered slider with a negative value and visible stop indicators at each end.

contentChunks.footer: Vertical centered slider
contentChunks.altText: Vertical centered slider with a negative value and visible stop indicators at each end.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Range sliders select two values on one slider to create a range. Use this when defining a minimum and maximum value.

Avoid using range sliders vertically, as this can add too much cognitive load. People are used to most sliders being horizontal.

contentChunks.footer: Horizontal range slider
contentChunks.altText: Horizontal range selection slider with 2 values selected, and a stop indicator at each end.

contentChunks.footer: Because of the additional cognitive load of a range slider, avoid using it in vertical orientation.
contentChunks.altText: Vertical range slider with 2 values selected, and a stop indicator at each end.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Anatomy

contentChunks.footer:
1. Value indicator (optional)
  2. Stop indicators (optional)
  3. Active track
  4. Handle
  5. Inactive track
  6. Inset icon (optional)
contentChunks.altText: 6 elements of a slider.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Track

The track shows the full range of values that can be selected on the slider. It has two sections: active and inactive.

  • The active section of the track is from the minimum value to the handle. For range sliders, the active track is between the two handles.
  • The inactive section of the track is from the handle to the maximum value, or outside the two handles of a range slider.

For left-to-right (LTR) languages, the values increase from left to right. For right-to-left (RTL) languages, this is reversed.

contentChunks.footer: The track on a slider shows the available range
contentChunks.altText: Sliders for font size and display size with stop indicators along the track.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Handle

The handle can be moved along the track to choose a value.

When sliders have two handles, the handles choose the minimum and maximum values in a range.

The handle changes shape to indicate when it’s pressed.

contentChunks.footer: A handle changes shape when it's being pressed or dragged
contentChunks.altText: The handle is a vertical line on the current value of the slider. It shrinks in width when selected.

contentChunks.footer: Two handles are used for sliders with range selection
contentChunks.altText: 2 unselected handles on a slider with range selection.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Configurations

Value

The value displays the specific value that corresponds with the handle’s placement. 

A value appears when interacting with the corresponding handle. For range sliders, only one value should be shown at a time.

If the value is shown elsewhere, the indicator is not required.

contentChunks.footer: A value can appear while the handle is being pressed or dragged
contentChunks.altText: A value of 50 is above a slider handle in the middle of the track.

contentChunks.footer: For range sliders, the value only appears on one handle at a time
contentChunks.altText: A value of 75 is above the pressed range slider handle. The unselected slider doesn’t show the value.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Instead of showing the built-in value label, a separate text input field can be added outside of the slider. If this is added, the slider and value in this text field should automatically update to match each other.

Make sure people can tab to the text field directly after the slider.

contentChunks.footer: Use Tab to navigate to values that are shown outside the slider, like a text input field
contentChunks.altText: Navigating to an adjacent text label, changing the value to 100 using arrow keys. The slider auto-updates based on input value.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Stop indicators

Stop indicators show which predetermined values can be chosen on the slider. The slider handle snaps to the closest stop. 

Avoid having too many stop indicators on a slider, because it can become visually crowded and difficult to adjust the value.

All sliders have stops at the end of the inactive track to ensure at least a 3:1 contrast with the background. If the inactive track has this level of contrast already, the end stops can be removed.

contentChunks.footer: Stop indicators show each available value on a slider
contentChunks.altText: Stop indicators are equally spaced out on a slider.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Icons or text can be added outside the slider to indicate the range of values and make the slider more accessible. This can be used instead of a stop indicator.

contentChunks.footer: Plus and minus icons, or text, can be added to the left and right of the slider
contentChunks.altText: Plus and minus icons on each end of the slider.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Orientation

Sliders can be oriented either horizontally or vertically, depending on what is best for your use case.

contentChunks.footer: Standard slider in horizontal orientation
contentChunks.altText: Horizontal slider.

contentChunks.footer: Standard slider in vertical orientation
contentChunks.altText: Vertical slider. Zero is at the bottom.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Inset icon

Standard sliders that are M, L, or XL can include an icon within the track. This icon should illustrate what the slider controls. Avoid adding inset icons to XS or S sliders.

When there’s not enough space for the icon on the active track, like at a low value, the icon moves to the inactive track.

Consider swapping which icon is displayed at zero, like a volume icon becoming a mute icon.

contentChunks.footer: Inset icons change placement based on the handle
contentChunks.altText: Inset icon on the active track when the handle is at 50%, and on the inactive track when the handle is at 0.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t use an inset icon with sliders that have track thicknesses under 40dp
contentChunks.altText: An inset icon on an XS slider. The icon bounds are cut off by the slider container.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Don’t use inset icons on centered or range sliders. It makes it unclear where the start of the slider is.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t use an inset icon on a centered slider
contentChunks.altText: Centered slider with an inset icon on one end, and a stop indicator on the other.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t use an inset icon on a range slider
contentChunks.altText: Range slider with an inset icon on one end, and a stop indicator on the other.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Size

Sliders come in different sizes: XS, S, M, L, and XL. Use larger sizes to increase the targets and provide a larger visual emphasis.

The active and inactive tracks should always be the same size.

contentChunks.footer:
1. XS: 16dp
  2. S: 24dp
  3. M: 40dp
  4. L: 56dp
  5. XL: 96dp
contentChunks.altText: 5 sizes of sliders.

contentChunks.htmlValue: XL sliders should be reserved for hero moments, where the slider itself is the most important element on the page.

contentChunks.footer: XL sliders should be the focus of the page
contentChunks.altText: An XL slider used to adjust living room temperature on mobile. No other controls are on screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Behaviors

Select & drag

Select a value by dragging the handle.

contentChunks.footer: Standard slider: The handle drags smoothly
contentChunks.altText: Slider handle moves smoothly. The value increases and decreases by single digits.

contentChunks.footer: Slider with stop indicators: The handle snaps to the closest stop indicator while dragged
contentChunks.altText: Slider handle snaps to the nearest multiple of 10 when moved.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Select jump

Select a value by selecting part of the track.

contentChunks.footer: Standard slider: The handle moves to the selected location
contentChunks.altText: Slider handle moves smoothly to selected value of the slider.

contentChunks.footer: Slider with stop indicators: The handle moves to the closest stop indicator
contentChunks.altText: Slider handle moves smoothly to the closest stop indicator value.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Select & arrow

Select a value using the keyboard.

Tab: Focus lands on handle 

Arrows: Selected value increases or decreases by one value or stop indicator

Space & arrows: Selected value increases or decreases by a larger interval or stop indicator

contentChunks.footer: Standard slider: The handle moves one value
contentChunks.altText: Tab selects the slider, and arrow keys move the value by 1.

contentChunks.footer: Slider with stop indicators: The handle moves to the next stop indicator
contentChunks.altText: Tab selects the slider, and arrow keys move the value by 10.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Use cases

People should be able to do the following using assistive technology:

  • Navigate to a slider 
  • Select a range by controlling a handle along a track
  • Get appropriate feedback based on input type
Interaction & style

The slider handle shrinks in width and the value appears to provide a visual cue to the user that the handle is being pressed.

Touch

When tapped or dragged, the handle width shrinks to provide interaction feedback, and the value appears.

Cursor

When hovered, the cursor changes. When clicked and dragged, the handle width shrinks, and the value appears.

contentChunks.footer: The slider handle changes width during interaction
contentChunks.altText: Dragging a slider using a mouse cursor and by touch. Handle width shrinks when dragged.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Focus and navigation

Initial focus lands directly on the handle, since it’s the primary interactive element of the slider.

The slider value can then be adjusted using the arrow keys or other keyboard navigation options.

contentChunks.footer: Use arrow keys to change the slider value
contentChunks.altText: Using keyboard navigation on a slider. Tab to the handle, and use arrow keys to change the value.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Color contrast
Use visual anchors so the end of the slider’s inactive track has at least 3:1 contrast with the background. The stop indicator makes the end easily visible on most backgrounds.

contentChunks.footer: A stop indicator on the inactive track makes it easier to identify the end of the slider on a low-contrast background
contentChunks.altText: The inactive track has contrast below 3:1 with the background. The stop indicator is above 3:1. Slider is accessible.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Alternatively, icons or other elements that have a 3:1 contrast with the background can be used to indicate the ends of the slider’s inactive track.

contentChunks.footer: Icons make it easier to identify the ends of the slider on a low-contrast background
contentChunks.altText: The inactive track has contrast ratio below 3:1 with the background. The icon is above 3:1. The slider is accessible.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Keyboard navigation

Keys
Actions
Tab
Moves focus to the slider handle
Arrows
Increase and decrease the value by one value or one stop indicator
Space & Arrows
Increase and decrease the value by one interval or one stop indicator
Home or End
Set the slider to the first and last values on the slider
Labeling elements
The accessibility label for a slider is typically the same as the slider's adjacent text label. It should have the slider role.

contentChunks.footer: A slider’s accessibility label should match the adjacent UI text
contentChunks.altText: Annotated aria tags of a slider.

contentChunks.htmlValue: If the UI text is correctly linked to the slider, assistive tech (such as a screenreader) will read the UI text followed by the component’s role.

contentChunks.footer: Icon buttons placed outside the slider should have the button role
contentChunks.altText: Annotated aria tags of a slider with stepper icons.
